clauses.title: A refused post-push revalidation is recomposed once and retried
requires: A refused post-push revalidation is recomposed once from a freshly taken post-push snapshot and retried

clauses.title: The builder derives the transition and refuses a head beside it
requires: is derived from pushes; it is not an input
pushes must be one to five post-push snapshots, oldest first
each push must be a snapshot result
each push snapshot must name its public head as a commit OID
each push snapshot must name one public head in both brackets

clauses.title: CL-D86 records both choices and the alarm reset
clauses.section: ## CL-D86 — The post-push revalidation is composed from the run's own snapshots
requires: *Owner choice:* Option A for both
issues/169#issuecomment-5786110213
The packaged-helper alarm resets from 270,000 to 280,000 bytes
retrying a refused revalidation more than once requires a new owner decision
A refused post-push revalidation is recomposed once from a freshly taken post-push snapshot and retried; a second refusal stops the run, and neither attempt consumes a gate or push counter.

The packaged autofix driver does not recompose a refused post-push revalidation: the first refusal, after the push or at the recheck before a later gate or the writer, stops the run `BLOCKED`, a gap CL-D112 first recorded, recorded and not closed (#249, CL-D117).

clauses.title: The CL-D86 fixtures pin the derivation, the refusals, and the alarm
requires: Issue #169 the transition is derived from the run
a head supplied by hand beside the snapshots is refused
the reset helper alarm is the one every suite asserts

clauses.title: The CLI declares the derived input and nothing else
requires: build_operator_revalidate: { required: ['captured', 'cwd'], optional: ['pushes'] }
